t:
(a) Designation.—The facility of the United States Postal Service located at 3050 Hunsinger Lane in Louisville, Kentucky, shall be known and designated as the “Iraq and Afghanistan Fallen Military Heroes of Louisville Memorial Post Office Building”. 
    (b) References.—Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the facility referred to in subsection (a) shall be deemed to be a reference to the “Iraq and Afghanistan Fallen Military Heroes of Louisville Memorial Post Office Building”.

fable.w: This section simply names a postal facility and deems references in federal records to refer to the new name. The word "regulation" appears only in boilerplate about existing records, not as a grant of rulemaking authority, and no outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue over any federal decision.
fable.s: shall be known and designated as the “Iraq and Afghanistan Fallen Military Heroes of Louisville Memorial Post Office Building”

qwen_block.w: This section simply designates a name for a federal facility and updates references to that facility. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public hearings, or comment periods mentioned.
qwen_block.s:
(a) Designation.—The facility of the United States Postal Service located at 3050 Hunsinger Lane in Louisville, Kentucky, shall be known and designated as the “Iraq and Afghanistan Fallen Military Heroes of Louisville Memorial Post Office Building”. 
    (b) References.—Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the facility referred to in subsection (a) shall be deemed to be a reference to the “Iraq and Afghanistan Fallen Military Heroes of Louisville Memorial Post Office Building”.

opus.w: The section only names a Postal Service building and says that references to it in existing records point to the new name. The word "regulation" might look like a grant of rulemaking power, but it only lists one kind of record that mentions the facility. It does not authorize any rulemaking. No one outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing or comment period, or given a right to sue over a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section simply designates a specific USPS facility with a commemorative name. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with people outside the federal government (such as the public, local governments, or experts) in making this decision. The designation is a legislative act, not a participatory process.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that naming a building after "Fallen Military Heroes" involves honoring people outside the government, or that the designation process might have involved local input. However, the text itself only mandates a change in the official name of a federal facility. It does not describe any process of consultation, public comment, or advisory input from outside parties. The decision is made by Congress through the statute itself.
